That background investigation confirms what I found empirically: only `load` (with an explicit `alias:`) can introduce a brand-new model alias mid-plan — `cast`'s `to` field can't, because `CastSpec.collect_models()` requires both endpoints to already be known aliases, so `validate_model_aliases` rejects an unregistered `to` alias before any inference runs. That matches the `unknown model alias: 'work'` error I hit and fixed by keeping scratch tensors under the already-declared `base` alias (`base::scratch.*`) instead.

No changes needed — the shipped `out/T4/plan.yaml` already works around this correctly and the output has been verified (244 tensors, bit-exact non-MLP, 0.0 relative error on the merge). This finding is just extra confirmation of the root cause noted in `out/T4/REPORT.md`.
